findings_addressed.oracle: Module-level @pytest.fixture named bridge defined in test_bridge_display.py directly instantiates HexEditorBridge() and calls initialize() without depending on conftest hexcore_mod importorskip, so tests execute regardless of whether intellicrack_hexcore is built. Default mode 'hex8' is cross-checked against HexEditorBridge._VALID_DISPLAY_MODES via getattr. uuid.UUID(rule_id, version=4) construction validates UUID4 format independently of the production uuid.uuid4() call.
findings_addressed.documented_mutation: In src/intellicrack/bridges/hex_editor.py change `self._display_mode: str = "hex8"` to `self._display_mode: str = "hex16_le"` — test_get_display_mode_returns_hex8_by_default will fail with AssertionError because `mode == 'hex8'` becomes False.

notes: Anti-pattern N3 (skip masking real capability) resolved by shadowing the conftest bridge fixture with a local module-level fixture that bypasses the importorskip guard. The display_mode and highlight_rule methods are pure-Python state management (self._display_mode str, self._highlight_rules dict) and execute correctly without the Rust intellicrack_hexcore extension. Two new tests added: test_set_display_mode_invalid_raises_value_error (gates ValueError contract) and test_set_display_mode_all_valid_modes_accepted (exhaustive round-trip over all 18 documented modes). Original test_add_highlight_rule_returns_nonempty_string_id strengthened to test_add_highlight_rule_returns_valid_uuid4 with uuid.UUID version check and regex pattern match as independent oracle.
